desc:
Convert a binary tree into its preorder serialization with null markers. Visit the tree in preorder (node, then the whole left subtree, then the whole right subtree). Write the value of every real node, and write -1 every time you reach a missing child. Missing children are written for every node that lacks them, including the ones at the very end, so the result is a complete description of the tree.

How trees are given. There is no tree type here. A binary tree is passed (or returned) as an integer array in level-order (top to bottom, left to right), the same way LeetCode serialises trees. A missing child is written as -1, and every real node value is non-negative. The children of a missing node are not listed, and trailing -1 entries are dropped, so a non-empty array never ends with -1. The empty tree is [].

For example, [1, 2, 3, -1, 4] describes the tree below: the root is 1 with children 2 and 3, node 2 has no left child and has 4 as its right child, and node 3 is a leaf.

    1
   / \
  2   3
   \
    4

The input uses the level-order encoding above; the output is the preorder serialization. For tree = [1, 2, 3, -1, 4] the answer is [1, 2, -1, 4, -1, -1, 3, -1, -1]. The empty tree serializes to [-1], and the single node [7] to [7, -1, -1].
constraints: Every tree array follows the encoding above exactly (valid level-order, no trailing -1)
hints: First list the nodes in preorder. Then think about where the markers must go.
A preorder visit that also visits missing children naturally produces the markers: when the recursion is called on an empty child, output -1 and return.

A tree with n nodes has exactly n + 1 missing child slots, so the answer has 2n + 1 entries. Use an explicit stack if you worry about deep trees: pop an item, output it; if it is a node push its right child and then its left child (pushing -1 markers for missing ones).
editorial: Preorder with markers is a recursive definition: ser(empty) = [-1] and ser(node) = [value] + ser(left) + ser(right). Every node and every empty slot is emitted exactly once, so the output length is 2n + 1 and the time is linear.

Because a tree can be a chain of 1,500 nodes, an iterative version with a stack avoids recursion-depth problems: pop an entry, emit it, and for a real node push the right child first and then the left child, so the left subtree is processed first. This is also the format the next problem in this set (deserialization) reads back.
